### MAP-06118417F5

- mapping source: [packages/uta-protocol/src/client/UTAClient.ts:31-35](../../../../packages/uta-protocol/src/client/UTAClient.ts#L31-L35)
- symbol: RequestOpts
- unique targetChapters: 3, 4, 8, 9, 14, 19
- id: MAP-06118417F5
- assessment: designed
- sourceEvidence:
  - packages/uta-protocol/src/client/UTAClient.ts:31-35: RequestOpts has body?: unknown, raw string/number/undefined params, and optional AbortSignal.
  - docs/uta-effect-runtime-design/solutions/composition-contract.md:K03/K05/K07: boundary controls are private, declared leaf schemas own public inputs, and interruption/deadline/error handling remains typed without turning data transport into a transaction.
  - docs/uta-effect-runtime-design/solutions/integration-decisions.md:C11: public transport is Promise&lt;Result&lt;Output, Failure&gt;&gt; plus AbortSignal, push is AsyncIterable, and local failure variants are fixed.
- currentBehavior: RequestOpts accepts arbitrary JSON and stringifies every query value; AbortSignal is the only structured control input.
- problem: Unknown body/query records allow invalid commands, unbounded parameters and accidental native objects; no typed distinction exists between query admission and command payload.
- targetModel: Keep private transport controls for AbortSignal and deadline, but make every public input a descriptor-declared schema instead of RequestOpts with unknown body and raw maps. Alice's public HTTP call returns Promise&lt;Result&lt;Output, Failure&gt;&gt;; caller cancellation and the internal deadline are composed, and push uses a declared AsyncIterable frame/control/error/close protocol with resource-scoped cancellation. A controlled effect interrupted after its durable send boundary remains outcome-unknown/recoverable rather than a rejection.
- pureTransitions:
  - Decode each leaf input from its own schema, keep AbortSignal/deadline private to the interpreter, and map caller cancellation to Cancelled or DeadlineExceeded without changing a post-send controlled effect into rejection; push cancellation closes only its declared resource.
- effectBoundary: Boundary decoding and cancellation are transport mechanics, while provider leaf inputs and stream controls are open declarations. Alice does not expose RequestOpts as a universal input record or expose internal Effect as a public dependency.
- durability: AbortSignal and deadline are ephemeral. A controlled leaf persists its own command identity and recovery evidence; pull/push data operations do not acquire order transaction state.
- errors:
  - Cancelled
  - DeadlineExceeded
  - TransportUnavailable
  - ProtocolViolation
  - RemoteBoundaryFailure
  - RemoteDomainFailure&lt;LeafError&gt;
  - UnknownAfterPossibleSend
- preservedBehavior:
  - Preserve cancellation semantics and omission of optional fields, but intentionally stop accepting arbitrary query keys/bodies and do not use caller cancellation to bypass the deadline.
- replacementSteps:
  - Replace public RequestOpts with descriptor-derived input/control types, expose Promise&lt;Result&lt;Output, Failure&gt;&gt; plus AbortSignal, and keep the signal/deadline composition only in the interpreter.
  - Migrate query, stream, and effect callers so cancellation, resource closure, and possible-send recovery are handled at their respective boundaries.
- verificationCases:
  - An unknown body/query key is rejected before fetch; a pull cancellation yields Cancelled or DeadlineExceeded according to the cause, a push cancellation closes only that resource, and interrupting after possible send remains unknown/recoverable.
  - A caller-supplied AbortSignal cannot disable the configured deadline, and a push consumer receives only declared AsyncIterable frames/control events.
- openQuestions: —
- contractDisposition: retained
- contractRationale: The source accepts unknown bodies and stringifies arbitrary query values, but its AbortSignal seam is valuable. C11 fixes the public Promise/AbortSignal and AsyncIterable shape plus local cancellation/deadline variants; K03/K05/K06/K07 retain boundary decoding and distinct pull/push/effect lifecycle without leaking raw maps.
- contractAnchors:
  - [K03](../composition-contract.md)
  - [K05](../composition-contract.md)
  - [K06](../composition-contract.md)
  - [K07](../composition-contract.md)
- review: accepted — UTAClient.ts:31-35 exposes unknown body/query values and AbortSignal; C11 fixes Promise/AbortSignal, AsyncIterable push, composed cancellation/deadline, and local Cancelled/DeadlineExceeded/TransportUnavailable/ProtocolViolation variants while preserving post-send recovery (K03/K05/K07/K08).

- currentBehavior: Prefix resolution preserves a matching trading account under the filter.
- problem: Prefix matching can be ambiguous and returns raw identity; it must not choose an implicit subaccount or infer action permissions.
- targetModel: Retain typed prefix resolution as a discovery projection with explicit ambiguity/not-found and resource-scope outcomes. A unique source match yields a provider/resource identity, not a default wallet or effect capability; subsequent calls discover the selected leaf and schema.
- pureTransitions:
  - source-prefix resolution: construct only schema-valid declared capability fixtures, feed them through the same boundary decoder, and assert observed semantic results rather than implementation casts or method counts.
- effectBoundary: The test fixture is a narrow provider/composition boundary. It may script declared data/effect outcomes, but it cannot stand in for native guarantees, durable storage, responsible agent delivery, or a complete broker implementation.
- durability: Fixture assertions do not prove production durability. Separate integration gates must exercise a real durable store/foreign process/agent or broker ledger when the scenario requires those facts.

  - Keep empirical obligations explicit and avoid a complete fake interface, universal Unsupported handlers, or optimistic fallback data.

  - Any claimed durable/foreign/native result is separately marked for the real implementation gate.

- contractDisposition: retained
- contractRationale: The source test preserves matching under tradingOnly, but raw prefix selection can be ambiguous and says nothing about subaccount or action authority. K02/K03/K06 retain the convenience while making scope and capability explicit.

- durability: Ordinary data is a rebuildable projection or resource-scoped stream. Only evidence deliberately selected for a later controlled effect is persisted with that effect; a cache/read failure does not create transaction recovery work.

  - The data path performs no prepare/approve/dispatch/compensation side effect.

## Cross-group contracts

- Shared dependency: docs/uta-effect-runtime-design/solutions/composition-contract.md; Capability composition boundary (K01/K02): Alice consumes the fixed CapabilityDescriptor outer metadata (identity, path, schema version/fingerprint, input/result/error schema references, delivery, effect category, resources, source, and availability evidence). Provider capability trees, leaf schemas, error vocabularies, and HOF composition remain open-ended; there is no global ActionContractMap, mandatory full broker handler product, or universal order route list. The MAP line ranges cited below are historical investigation anchors pinned to audit commit a5f23756531cc552b7e12b6d655ae1ffbcd28b64; re-read current source before implementation. Evidence: packages/uta-protocol/src/client/UTAClient.ts:22-35; src/services/uta-client/UTAAccountSDK.ts:72-389; src/services/uta-client/UTAManagerSDK.ts:41-244.
- Shared dependency: docs/uta-effect-runtime-design/solutions/composition-contract.md; Schema and foreign-process boundary (K03/K07): Alice decodes unknown only at the transport edge and invokes schema-fingerprinted capability handles. Static provider declarations retain exact types; dynamic providers expose validated schema descriptions. IBKR Contract/ContractDescription and other native values remain adapter-internal. The source IBroker/global switch, where documented elsewhere, remains source evidence and is not a target requirement to reproduce or erase.
- Shared dependency: docs/uta-effect-runtime-design/solutions/composition-contract.md; Data delivery boundary (K04/K05): Instrument, Candle, News, NewsGroup, account facts, orders, fills, FX, and health observations are semantic data units when their leaves exist. Pull returns a finite declared result; push is a resource-scoped stream with frame/control/close/error semantics. Data reads, caches, and streams do not use order prepare/approve/compensate/WAL; selected evidence may be persisted only when deliberately consumed by a controlled effect.
- Shared dependency: docs/uta-effect-runtime-design/solutions/composition-contract.md; Resource/projection boundary (K02/K05): AccountScope is required only for a capability whose resource is account/subaccount scoped; aggregate versus scoped selectors are explicit when a provider declares both. Listings and projections retain Complete/Partial/Unavailable, checkpoint/freshness, and source evidence. Missing scope, unavailable data, and structural capability absence never become a default wallet or fabricated empty result.
- Shared dependency: docs/uta-effect-runtime-design/solutions/composition-contract.md; Controlled-effect boundary (K08/K09/K11): withTransaction is optional and wraps only provider leaves that perform controlled trading mutations requiring durable intent/approval/dispatch/recovery. Order is a semantic unit with provider-native exact extension schemas; no Cartesian handwritten order variants or universal Place/Modify/Cancel/Close contract is imposed. Existing intent/revision, approval, WAL/CAS/idempotency, lease, reconciliation, Unknown, and non-ACID compensation obligations remain inside this wrapper only; data and ordinary admin paths do not acquire them.
- Shared dependency: docs/uta-effect-runtime-design/solutions/composition-contract.md; Trigger/review boundary (K09/K10): an event/stream source is evidence, not authority. If Alice exposes a trigger or review capability, ReturnToAgent atomically consumes the activation, pauses the binding, retains unsent intent/evidence, and emits a durable ReviewRequest/outbox with zero broker dispatch. Keep/rearm/revise/discard/request-submission are explicit schemas; Workspace/Session/Inbox delivery and agent receipt are outside this client.
- Shared dependency: docs/uta-effect-runtime-design/solutions/composition-contract.md; Lifecycle, admin, and test boundary (K01/K07/K11/K12): no-op helpers are removed or replaced by an actually declared admin/lifecycle/test capability. Guardian/process restart, provider connection recovery, snapshot scheduling, clocks, and CCXT registration remain owned by their runtime/composition authority and are not account-proxy promises. Tests prove descriptor composition and falsifiable boundaries, not native guarantees or durable execution by casted fakes.
- Shared dependency: docs/uta-effect-runtime-design/solutions/composition-contract.md; Evidence obligations (K11/K12): retain source facts about generic casts, Git/pending-hash compatibility, empty fallbacks, raw errors, precision/time handling, paper/read-only behavior, and provider-native uncertainty. A descriptor abstraction does not resolve native idempotency, absence, finality, atomicity, delivery, or redaction evidence; those remain implementation-gate obligations in the owning provider/runtime designs.

## Additional findings

- The runtime schema barrel remains empty at packages/uta-protocol/src/schemas/index.ts:1-10. Main must provide the shared descriptor/envelope codec path before treating any Alice response as trusted; this is a schema/runtime prerequisite, not evidence that every provider shares one DTO.
- Contract search at services/uta/src/http/routes-trading.ts:149-164 normalizes assetClass/source/accountId and returns flat hits. Alice must preserve source identity, selector/completeness, and the declared catalog leaf; the current flat route is source evidence, not a universal target shape.
- Historical data at services/uta/src/http/routes-trading.ts:343-360 revives Date and maps broker failures to raw 500. The data leaf must declare temporal/Decimal/Candle schema and quality/partial/error evidence; it must remain a finite pull and not inherit order transaction state.
- Wallet push/reject at services/uta/src/http/routes-trading.ts:443-495 use pending hashes and PENDING_HASH_CONFLICT. Preserve this as compatibility evidence only; a controlled-effect leaf may replace it with descriptor-bound command identity/revision/digest, while providers without that effect leaf remain structurally absent.
- The tool wall at src/tool/trading.ts:184-198 and :203-207,760-807 stages an order and supplies allowAiTrading. Alice must expose draft versus controlled-effect capability composition; allowAiTrading and callbacks are policy/preflight inputs and cannot self-authorize or turn a read-only preview into execution.
- src/tool/trading.ts:440-450 falls back to getPendingOrderIds while UTAAccountSDK.ts:371-375 returns []. Main must migrate to a declared order-observation capability with explicit completeness; data projection remains separate from order execution.
- Startup policy at src/main.ts:120-156 and source selection in src/tool/trading.ts are product inputs. Descriptor discovery and withTransaction authorization remain authoritative; tier/source inclusion does not prove query, draft, approval, or execution capability.
- services/uta/src/http/routes-trading.ts:261-292 exposes scoped and aggregate subaccount behavior. The capability input must state the selected resource/aggregate semantics when the provider declares both; omitted subAccountId is not a universal default-wallet convention.
